items.label: Hedge-correlation subagent took ~22 minutes this run (vs the usual few minutes) -- rate-limit contention plus a self-caught data-integrity bug, not a data-quality problem in the final numbers
items.detail: This run launched the hedge-correlation subagent alongside 3 track-record pricing subagents and 2 research subagents, all sharing the same IBKR connector rate limit (10/sec, 30/min) -- the pricing subagents repeatedly hit and reported that limit explicitly, needing several resumes each. The correlation subagent eventually completed and reported that its initial batched fetch of all 19 one-year price histories came back in a different order than requested (caught by cross-checking one series against an individually-fetched version); rather than risk mis-assigning tickers to clusters, it re-verified all 19 series individually by exact-value-matching before computing any correlation -- the figures in hedge_analysis/diversification_actions above reflect that fully re-verified data, not the suspect initial batch.
items.recommendation: In future runs, consider staggering the hedge-correlation subagent to run alone or first, before launching the higher-volume track-record pricing subagents, to avoid this kind of rate-limit-driven slowdown. No action needed on the data itself -- it was caught and corrected before use.
